open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that one finite common-ray library has vanishing face-to-cone Gaussian-weighted discrepancy while simultaneously preserving semantic coverage and separated risk uniformly over every translated mean.
open_obligations.obstruction: Commutativity yields a path-independent product of averaging operators, but it does not bound the difference between a face rule and the incident cone rule obtained by adding a ray average. For an arbitrary bounded ancestor this difference can remain of order one on a fixed Gaussian neighborhood as the averaging length grows. The available translation estimate controls shifts of the averaged rule itself, and one-sided recession averaging preserves coverage only along labelwise recession directions; neither fact supplies the required simultaneous global separated-risk comparison.
open_obligations.attempted: The established route starts from one Gaussian-smoothed ancestor, uses a common rational simplicial fan with literally shared one-dimensional Folner factors, shares finite-element variables on common faces, reports the full label set on transition bands, and applies weighted path telescoping. This closes the operator cocycle, incidence-path independence, and translation boundary ratios, but no valid step turns those facts into a vanishing face-to-cone discrepancy or a uniform translated-mean risk bound.
